Generate a prioritization

Source: R/fct_prioritization.R
prioritization.Rd

Generate a prioritization using multi-objective optimization techniques.

Usage

prioritization(project, settings, gap = 0.1, solver = "cbc", verbose = FALSE)

Arguments

project

[new_project()] object. These data are used to specify the underlying data for generating the solution.

settings

`list` object with settings for generating a solution. See Settings format section for further details.

gap

`numeric` value denoting optimality gap. Defaults to 0.1 (10% from optimality).

solver

`character` value indicating the name of the software used for optimization. Acceptable values include `"gurobi"` or `"cbc"`. Defaults to `"cbc"`.

verbose

`logical` value indicating if information should be displayed during optimization process. Defaults to `FALSE`.

Value

A `list` with a `solution` element that contains a `numeric` vector with values indicating the zone for each planning unit, and a `results` element that contains supplementary information.

Settings format

The argument to `settings` must be a `list` with the following elements.

features

A `data.frame` with the theme and feature settings. These are used to specify the targets and weights considered for the features during optimization. Each row corresponds to a different feature, and it must have the following columns: `"id"`, `"name"`, `"column"`, `"zone"`, `"target"`, and `"weight"`. Note that target values must be expressed as a proportion (i.e., value between zero and one).

locks

A `data.frame` with the settings to specify which locks are used to lock in planning units to a particular zone. Each row corresponds to a different lock, and it must have the following columns: `"id"`, `"name"`, `"column"`, and `"zone"`.

costs

A `data.frame` with the cost settings. These are used to specify which costs are considered for each zone. Each row corresponds to a different cost, and it must have the following columns: `"id"`, `"name"`, `"zone"`, and `"weight"`.

zones

A `data.frame` with settings for the multi-objective optimization. Each row corresponds to a different zone, and it must have the following columns: `"name"` and `"weight"`.

Examples

# simulate data
project <- simulate_project()
#> Error in simulate_project(): could not find function "simulate_project"
solver_settings <- simulate_prioritization_settings(project)
#> Error in simulate_prioritization_settings(project): could not find function "simulate_prioritization_settings"

# preview settings
print(solver_settings)
#> Error: object 'solver_settings' not found

# generate solution
sol <- prioritization(project, solver_settings)
#> Error in prioritization(project, solver_settings): could not find function "prioritization"

# preview solution
print(sol)
#> Error: object 'sol' not found
